Thanks for the demo today, Tessa — appreciate the walkthrough. A quick recap from our side and a couple of clarifying questions so we can vet this with security and procurement: 

- We handle PHI and will need a signed BAA. Our security team also wants to see your SOC2 Type II report and a short artifact list (encryption at rest, audit logs, key management).
- Primary question: Is Redwood's Hosted API (with a signed BAA) considered a supported production route for customers with PHI, or do we need Redwood Dedicated / Private VPC to meet our compliance posture? We want to know the tradeoffs: e.g., latency, responsibility split, evidence you can provide.
- Procurement timeline: we're aiming for a vendor decision by end of July; can you tell me what docs you can provide this week and whether you can sign a BAA on standard terms?

Hi Emma — great to meet you earlier, and thanks for the clear RFP excerpt. Quick post-demo recap and proposed next steps below. I included Marissa (CS lead) and Karthik (infra/solutions) to help with the technical evidence.

Recap of deployment options (short):
- Hosted API + BAA: Supported for many PHI customers. We provide a signed BAA, SOC2 Type II report, encryption at rest, audit logging, and customer-level isolation. Best for fastest time-to-value and pay-as-you-go pricing.
- Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity): Dedicated GPU pools, predictable throughput, and stronger isolation guarantees — typically used when customers require isolated capacity or stricter contractual SLAs.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): Full control plane in your VPC or on-prem package for regulated workloads that mandate it. Longer lead time and higher TCO but minimizes shared-infrastructure concerns.

What we can deliver this week:
- SOC2 summary and the SOC2 Type II report (redacted) — attached.
- BAA template for your legal review — attached (we can sign standard PayCare terms but may suggest a couple of narrow redlines around liability caps).
- A short evidence checklist for encryption, key management, and audit logs (I put that in the Drive link).

Suggested next steps: 
1) Security: Can your InfoSec team review the attached SOC2 summary and BAA this week? If yes, please share one or two availability windows for a follow-up call.
2) Procurement: if you prefer Hosted API + BAA, we can prepare pricing and a 30-day PoC agreement for your legal/procurement by next Tuesday. If you prefer Dedicated or Private, we’ll need to scope capacity and lead times — let us know which direction and we’ll loop infra.
3) Technical: Karthik flagged two items to confirm: encryption key ownership (customer KMS vs Redwood-hosted) and required retention period for logs — can you share the target retention and whether you need HSM-backed keys?

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2-summary.pdf, Redwood_BAA-template.docx

Thanks — happy to align on a short call if that helps.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Karthik — forwarding the thread. Quick internal notes for the PoC conversation: 

- If PayCare wants Hosted API, plan is: enable per-account encryption with customer KMS (we can support AWS KMS or GCP KMS), enable audit log export to their Cloud Storage, and scope throughput for 50k tokens/day initially.
- For Dedicated: we should size a small reserved capacity (1–2 A100 eqv) for the first quarter and propose a canary rollout (start hosted sandbox → prod on dedicated if latency/throughput needs arise).
- For Private/VPC: estimate 6–8 week lead time for initial deployment and network validation.

Karthik — can you confirm: 1) we support bringing your own KMS for Hosted API; 2) default audit logs retention is 90 days but can be extended to 1 year with the premium observability add-on; and 3) do we have a redacted SOC2 we can share as-is or does legal want an additional cover note?

Thanks — will join the follow-up with Emma if needed.

-Marissa
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
